annotation.kind: source selection, tier label, linked stable product computation, and explicit first-order projection for equation (8)

assumptions: The matrix dimension is positive and the exact and computed operands are real square n-by-n matrices, as in equation (1) and the recursive-inversion application of equation (8).
One otherwise unspecified matrix norm is used throughout and satisfies nonnegativity, definiteness, homogeneity, subadditivity, and submultiplicativity.
Machine epsilon is positive; mu is nonnegative and has a finite polynomial-growth certificate, matching the normwise stable-multiplication model surrounding equation (1).
The computed product is linked exactly to the two perturbed operands, one local first-order multiplication error, and one explicitly bounded epsilon-squared remainder.
The left and right operand perturbation norms are bounded by their respective nonnegative inherited absolute errors.

The selected first-order error removes the inherited-error cross product and local higher-order remainder from the full realized product error; no exceptional-value semantics are added beyond the paper's real-valued normwise model.

conditions.L: The identical fixed statement and P10 shared files are present; the frozen NumStability library is also present.
conditions.N: The fixed statement and P10 shared files are present; no NumStability artifact is present.

formal_statement.lean_header: theorem p10_t2_first_order_product_error {n : Nat} (run : P10FirstOrderProductRun n) : run.matrixNorm.value (p10FirstOrderProductError run) <= p10FirstOrderProductErrorBudget run
formal_statement.plain_language: For one linked stable matrix-product computation, the realized first-order absolute normwise error is bounded by exactly the local multiplication term and the two cross-oriented inherited-input terms printed in equation (8).

informal_proof: Use the linked computed-product equation to cancel the inherited cross term and explicit epsilon-squared remainder, obtaining the exact first-order sum localError + A*dB + dA*B. Apply the selected norm's triangle inequality twice and submultiplicativity to the two propagated products, then substitute the local and inherited-error certificates.
informal_statement: Equation (8)'s complete three-term first-order absolute normwise product-error rule, with exact/computed operands linked and every omitted higher-order term represented outside the bounded first-order projection.
paper_version: published journal version; volume 108, 2007, printed pages 59-91

tier_rationale: The proof combines the local stable-multiplication certificate, both inherited-error certificates, two abstract submultiplicative bounds, and repeated subadditivity after a paper-specific noncommutative first-order extraction. The L proof obtains that extraction through NumStability.matMul_add_left and NumStability.matMul_add_right from the frozen MatrixAlgebra module. Searches across all 24 mounted modules found no declaration giving equation (8)'s linked three-term bound; the closer source-only MatMulFirstOrderSpec is not mounted, while the mounted Frobenius and entrywise results would improperly change the source's unnamed norm semantics.
